userFlows.name: Google Login Happy Path
userFlows.description: An existing registered user logs in via Google and is redirected to the dashboard.

userFlows.name: Failed Google Authentication
userFlows.description: A user attempts to log in but Google returns an error or authentication fails, redirecting the user back with an error message.

assumptions.text: We match Google accounts to existing app accounts using the email address returned by Google.
assumptions.impact: If our database matches solely on the email string without verifying that Google has actually validated that email address, we open up a critical account takeover vulnerability.

assumptions.text: Unregistered users trying to log in with Google should be blocked or shown an error rather than having an account auto-created.
assumptions.impact: The requirements specifically state 'As a registered user'. If we automatically create accounts for any Google login, we're violating the current scope and altering our user acquisition metrics.

risks.reason: If Google returns 'email_verified: false' in the payload and we still log the user in, anyone can register a dummy Google account with a target's email and hijack their account in our system.
If we don't validate the 'state' parameter in the OAuth callback, users are vulnerable to login CSRF attacks where an attacker forces a victim to log into the attacker's account.
If Google's authorization servers are down or slow, our application could hang or show unhelpful raw error dumps to the user.

tests.title: Successful login with existing verified email matches account and redirects to dashboard
preconditions: A user exists in our database with email 'testuser@gmail.com'.
Google OAuth sandbox environment is configured.
steps: Navigate to the login page.
Click the 'Log in with Google' button.
Authenticate using the mock Google account 'testuser@gmail.com'.
Allow redirects to complete.
tests.expectedResult: The user is successfully authenticated, a session is created, and they land on the '/dashboard' route.
tests.rationale: This is the primary happy path. We need to verify that we successfully link the incoming Google email with our existing record and create a valid local session.

tests.title: Reject login if Google email is not verified
preconditions: A user exists in our database with email 'unverified@gmail.com'.
steps: Mock a Google token response containing 'email': 'unverified@gmail.com' and 'email_verified': false.
Send this token payload to our OAuth callback endpoint.
tests.expectedResult: The server rejects the authentication attempt, does not establish a session, and returns a 401 Unauthorized status with a clear error payload.
tests.rationale: If we don't check the 'email_verified' flag from Google, anyone can create a free Google account with our users' emails and bypass password security to hijack accounts.

tests.title: OAuth callback rejects request with missing or mismatched state parameter
preconditions: An active OAuth flow session has been initiated.
steps: Send a request to our OAuth callback endpoint with either a missing 'state' query parameter or one that doesn't match the session state.
tests.expectedResult: The server rejects the request with a 400 Bad Request or 403 Forbidden, preventing login CSRF.
tests.rationale: Without state parameter validation, an attacker can trick a user into linking their session to an attacker's account.

tests.title: Unregistered user attempting Google login is shown an account-not-found error
preconditions: No user exists in our database with the email 'stranger@gmail.com'.
steps: Navigate to the login page.
Click 'Log in with Google'.
Authenticate with 'stranger@gmail.com'.
Wait for redirect back to our app.
tests.expectedResult: The user is redirected back to the login page and sees a visible error banner indicating that no registered account matches this Google profile.
tests.rationale: The requirement specifically targets existing registered users ('As a registered user...'). We must ensure we don't accidentally register new users automatically unless that is an explicitly approved feature.

tests.title: Graceful failure handling when Google API returns an error status
preconditions: Our server is configured to handle Google OAuth callback requests.
steps: Simulate an error response from Google during the OAuth callback (e.g., error=access_denied).
tests.expectedResult: The system redirects the user to the login page with a friendly error message, avoiding unhandled exceptions or raw stack traces.
tests.rationale: Users sometimes click 'Cancel' on Google's permission screen. We need to handle this gracefully instead of throwing a generic 500 error page.

requirement: As a registered user, I want to log in using Google so that I can access my account without entering a password.
acceptanceCriteria:
AC-001: User can initiate Google login.
AC-002: Successful authentication redirects to the dashboard.
AC-003: Existing users are associated with their account.
AC-004: Authentication failure displays an error.
implementationSummary: Added Google OAuth authentication, callback handling, account lookup and session creation.
